Photo conversion third-party software

The package's src/lib/libheif-without-unsafe-eval.js identifies its bundled
decoder as libheif 1.23.7 with LIBDE265_VERSION=1.0.16:

LGPL-3.0-or-later. Source: https://github.com/strukturag/libheif
Licence: libheif-COPYING.txt and GPL-3.0.txt in this directory.

libde265: Copyright (c) 2013-2014 struktur AG, Dirk Farin and contributors.
LGPL-3.0-or-later. Source: https://github.com/strukturag/libde265
Licence: libde265-COPYING.txt and GPL-3.0.txt in this directory.

The generated decoder includes Emscripten runtime support.
Copyright (c) 2010-2014 Emscripten authors. MIT OR NCSA.
Source: https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten
Licence: Emscripten-LICENSE.txt in this directory.

Our photo-preparation worker imports heic-to/csp in a separate app bundle.
The package embeds its decoder as JavaScript (wasm2js), starts a nested
blob-URL worker, and creates a bitmap without an intermediate full-size
canvas. There is no external script or WebAssembly download. The app worker
and its module dependencies load from the app's own origin; blob workers
contain that already-bundled code. Photos stay on the device for conversion.

These libraries are separate from the Household CFO application. Their
licences permit replacement or modification under their own terms; no
restriction is placed on reverse engineering for debugging modifications
to these libraries. Source/build instructions are available at the links
above. The app's separate worker bundle can be rebuilt with a replacement
heic-to package without changing the financial review code.
